name: vmware-workstation
description: Manage VMware Workstation with vmrun, REST, LAN segments, direct headless VNC/RFB console screenshots and input, and optional serial consoles.
long_description: Independent community integration for native VMware Workstation on Windows and Linux (Claude Desktop Linux is beta). VMware Workstation must be installed locally. Inventory requires no credentials. REST requires vmrest and local credentials; guest operations require VMware Tools and guest credentials. VNC consoles require per-VM authenticated loopback setup. Runs as your local user using stdio and opens no new network listener. Encryption and vTPM provisioning are unsupported.

tools.name: a_vmware_catalog
tools.description: Read running plugin version, process identity and complete registered tool names without VMware or credentials. Optionally compare assistant-visible names to diagnose missing tools, including an alphabetical cutoff. Cannot refresh the client catalog.

tools.name: a_vmware_mutate
tools.description: Call a discovered state-changing VMware operation when its direct tool is missing. First obtain its schema from a_vmware_catalog. Requires authorization for exact target/effects, confirm=true and every original confirmation. Reuses original validation, locks, credentials and handler; never retries. Do not bypass intentional policy.

tools.name: a_vmware_query
tools.description: Call a discovered read-only VMware operation when its direct tool is missing. First use a_vmware_catalog with tool to obtain the original strict argument schema. Reuses the same handler, deadlines, cancellation and redaction. Cannot call mutations or arbitrary commands; never bypass intentional policy.

tools.name: vm_security_capabilities
tools.description: Read-only native worker/version and vmcli help discovery. Separates installed tools from a verified encryption/vTPM backend. No security mutations or encryption modes are supported; no VM or credentials are opened.

tools.name: vm_security_status
tools.description: Read selected allowlisted VM security declarations without returning encryption keys, TPM contents or arbitrary VMX values. Encryption state/mode and actual vTPM presence remain unknown without independent native verification. No unlock, power or configuration changes.

tools.name: lab_validate
tools.description: Read-only versioned multi-VM lab validation and plan. Reuses template/hardware preflight, checks dependency graph, network/media mappings and aggregate disk space. Plans private LANs without creating them. No OS installation or readiness is implied.

tools.name: lab_deploy
tools.description: Plan by default. Explicit dry_run=false and confirm=true create a NEW lab root, private ownership manifest, optional owned LAN segments and blank template VMs. start=true opts into headless dependency/readiness-ordered startup. resume=true requires the identical recipe and bindings; completed verified VMs are skipped and uncertain partial creation is refused. No implicit rollback, overwrite or registration.

tools.name: lab_status
tools.description: Read the selected private lab manifest and observe VM ownership/power. Completed steps and uncertain intents are separate from live guest readiness. Does not scan for or adopt resources.

tools.name: lab_start
tools.description: Plan by default; explicit dry_run=false and confirm=true start only verified lab VMs headlessly in dependency order. Bounded Tools/IP/service readiness gates dependents; retries apply only to read-only readiness observations. Already running VMs are rechecked. No automatic replay of VM creation or power commands.

tools.name: lab_stop
tools.description: Plan by default; explicit dry_run=false and confirm=true stop only verified lab VMs in reverse dependency order. Soft shutdown is default, hard stop requires explicit mode=hard authorization. No hard fallback. Partial or uncertain outcomes remain in the manifest.

tools.name: lab_destroy
tools.description: Plan by default; explicit dry_run=false and confirm=true remove only recorded lab files and owned LAN segments. Requires fully offline, unlocked VMs; never stops implicitly. Refuses changed identity, links, external backings and uncertain creation. Keeps unknown files, empty member directories and the recovery manifest; never deletes external networks, media or unrelated files.

tools.name: template_list
tools.description: List bundled portable versioned JSON templates for Linux, Windows Server and nested ESXi. Returns complete editable recipes without reading host files or credentials.

tools.name: template_validate
tools.description: Read-only template validation and deployment plan: checks schema, supported installed hardware/disk capabilities, explicit local network/ISO bindings, new destination, allowlists and conservative free space. Shows VMX, disk paths and resource requirements. Reserves nothing.

tools.name: template_export
tools.description: Read an offline VM as a portable blank hardware recipe. Caller supplies new identity. Omits disk contents, UUIDs/MACs, host paths, network identity, secrets and arbitrary VMX fields; requires explicit local rebinding. Does not save a file or clone a guest.

tools.name: template_deploy
tools.description: Plan by default (dry_run=true). Real deployment requires dry_run=false and confirm=true after authorization. Creates blank sparse disks and VMX in a NEW directory with repeated preflight; never overwrites. Optional register/power_on default false. Partial files and failed post-actions are retained; inspect before retrying. No OS installation, vTPM/encryption or forced boot order.

tools.name: vm_hardware_capabilities
tools.description: Inspect installed native Workstation product version and conservative typed hardware limits. No power or configuration changes. vTPM writes require an unavailable encryption backend; nested CPU and guest driver support remain unverified.

tools.name: vm_hardware_get
tools.description: Read typed declared CPU topology, memory, nested virtualization, firmware/security, storage and NIC configuration. Omits unrelated VMX secrets and does not infer missing values or claim live device support.

tools.name: vm_hardware_set
tools.description: Apply explicit typed offline hardware changes with VMX backup and concurrency checks. Requires confirm=true, supported installed worker, full power-off and closed VMware GUI. Preserves omitted devices and NIC identity; no disk replacement, encryption or vTPM mutation.

tools.name: iso_list
tools.description: Inspect optical devices, ISO backings and configured connection/start-connected state. Does not claim live connection state or mount anything.

tools.name: iso_mount
tools.description: Attach an existing allowlisted local ISO to an optical or unused IDE/SATA slot, with VMX backup. Requires confirm=true and fully powered-off, unlocked VM. Refuses ambiguous devices and occupied disk slots. No live hot-swap or power-on.

tools.name: iso_eject
tools.description: Disable the selected optical device and remove its backing path, with VMX backup. Requires confirm=true and full power-off. Preserves ISO files, controller and unrelated devices. A later mount re-enables the slot.

tools.name: vm_boot_status
tools.description: Inspect firmware/boot VMX values and installed vmrun version. Boot-order and next-boot firmware writes report unsupported until installed-version compatibility is proven; no configuration or power changes.

tools.name: vm_boot_configure
tools.description: Request boot-order or next-boot firmware configuration. Currently fails explicitly with UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY and writes nothing: no installed-version-verified headless backend is available.

tools.name: guest_exec
tools.description: Execute an explicitly authorized guest program with literal arguments or an explicit interpreter/script using a required local credential profile. Captures bounded redacted stdout/stderr and verifies exit codes through a unique completion record. Requires Tools and Python 3 on Linux or Windows PowerShell 5.1. Transport success alone never means guest success. Timeout/cancellation may leave a running guest process; never retry automatically.

tools.name: vm_wait_for_boot
tools.description: Wait for VMware Tools running in the selected VM, indicating OS agent readiness only. Power-on, login and application readiness are separate. Bounded total timeout, polling and MCP cancellation; never starts a VM.

tools.name: vm_wait_for_ip
tools.description: Wait for a valid guest IP published by VMware Tools. Does not establish network reachability or service readiness. Bounded total timeout and cancellation; never starts a VM.

tools.name: vm_wait_for_service
tools.description: Probe only the selected VM Tools-reported IP and explicit port. TCP means connection accepted; HTTP(S) means expected status, with no redirects or retained body/headers. Does not execute guest commands. Bounded deadline and cancellation.

tools.name: vm_get_recent_errors
tools.description: Read bounded current vmware.log data only after verifying its selected VM identity. Returns normalized error excerpts and actions; arbitrary log text/paths/secrets are omitted. No host log scan.

tools.name: vm_collect_diagnostics
tools.description: Save selected VM allowlisted hardware, lifecycle, Tools/IP, snapshot count and normalized log excerpts into a NEW approved directory. Optional direct VNC guest pixels are unredacted: review before sharing. Never captures host desktop or executes guest commands.

tools.name: serial_status
tools.description: Inspect optional per-VM serial capability/configuration and session state without connecting or starting a VM. Only a connected session proves native endpoint ownership.

tools.name: serial_configure
tools.description: Explicitly replace or disable one serial port configuration in a powered-off unlocked VMX, with a backup. Requires confirm=true after authorization. Uses only a generated per-VM local pipe/socket; never starts a VM.

tools.name: serial_connect
tools.description: Explicitly connect to the configured VM serial pipe/socket after verifying native VMware ownership. Guest serial output must be enabled separately. No host terminal, desktop or remote TCP access.

tools.name: serial_read
tools.description: Read at most max_bytes from an explicitly connected VM serial port. Bounded wait returns timed_out with empty data. Base64 preserves bytes; UTF-8 also returns raw_base64. MCP cancellation preserves unread bytes.

tools.name: serial_write
tools.description: Send 1-65536 UTF-8 or canonical base64 bytes to an explicitly connected VM serial port. Can change guest state; requires authorization for the intended input. Timeout/cancellation may leave partial input; never replay automatically.

tools.name: serial_disconnect
tools.description: Close this VM serial session, cancel pending I/O and discard its buffer. Does not stop the VM or change its serial hardware.

tools.name: console_screenshot
tools.description: Capture a fresh PNG from this VM native VNC/RFB framebuffer. Never captures the host desktop. Works during BIOS/UEFI, PXE and installation without VMware Tools.

tools.name: console_click
tools.description: Click VM framebuffer coordinates using a direct RFB PointerEvent. No host mouse, window activation or desktop focus is used.

tools.name: console_key
tools.description: Send a named key or chord to this VM via RFB, for example F2, Escape, Enter, ArrowDown, Ctrl+Alt+Delete. No host keyboard input is used.

tools.name: console_type
tools.description: Type text into the VM via RFB key events, including at pre-OS prompts. Does not use the clipboard, guest agents, or host keyboard injection. Guest keyboard layout affects text.

tools.name: console_scroll
tools.description: Send RFB wheel events to the VM at the last console pointer position or framebuffer center. amount is the number of wheel ticks.

tools.name: console_status
tools.description: Check this VM native loopback-only VNC configuration and authenticated RFB session. Does not start the VM or modify its VNC settings.

tools.name: create_vm
tools.description: Create a new blank VMX and sparse virtual disk in a NEW directory using VMware Virtual Disk Manager. Configure CPUs, memory, firmware, networking and optional ISO. Does not install a guest OS or power on/register the VM.

tools.name: configure_vm
tools.description: Edit a powered-off UTF-8 VMX with a backup. Set arbitrary VMX key/value strings or null to remove keys. Refuses running, locked, or detected suspended VMs. Use for CPU, memory, boot media, network and other VMX configuration.

tools.name: disk_manager_status
tools.description: Discover native VMware Virtual Disk Manager and the exact flags/disk types advertised by its installed help. Missing capabilities return actionable status.

tools.name: disk_inspect
tools.description: Read a local VMDK descriptor, capacity, extents and backing-chain metadata. No disk-manager repair, guest mount or filesystem access.

tools.name: disk_create
tools.description: Create a local VMDK in a NEW parent directory to protect companion extents. Supports installed growable/preallocated single/split disk types 0-3.

tools.name: disk_expand
tools.description: Expand an independent offline VMDK to total capacity_mb. Requires explicit confirmation; refuses snapshots, locks, shared/backing chains. Does not resize guest partitions or filesystems.

tools.name: disk_convert
tools.description: Convert an independent offline local VMDK into a NEW parent directory, preserving the original. Supports advertised types 0-3 and stream-optimized output type 5. Partial output is retained on failure.

tools.name: disk_compact
tools.description: Compact an independent offline growable VMDK using installed -k capability. Requires explicit confirmation. Guest free-space preparation is separate; no guest filesystem resize.

tools.name: disk_defragment
tools.description: Defragment an independent offline growable VMDK using installed -d capability. Requires explicit confirmation and conservative free-space checks.

tools.name: disk_attach
tools.description: Attach an independent VMDK to an existing controller and explicit unused unit in a powered-off VMX, with a backup. Refuses snapshots, locked/suspended VMs and known shared disks. confirm requires authorization.

tools.name: disk_detach
tools.description: Remove the explicit VMX disk slot after verifying its expected VMDK, with a backup. Never deletes the underlying VMDK or extents. Requires authorization and a powered-off snapshot-free VM.

tools.name: ovf_tool_status
tools.description: Discover optional local VMware OVF Tool, version and supported flags. VMWARE_OVFTOOL_PATH overrides automatic discovery with an absolute executable path.

tools.name: ovf_inspect
tools.description: Start a read-only background appliance probe. job_status.result reports hardware, disks, NICs, properties, deployment options and manifest checks. Local flat OVF/OVA packages only.

tools.name: ovf_validate
tools.description: Start read-only local OVF/OVA schema and manifest validation. Returns a job ID. Remote-host compatibility, signer trust and guest boot are not established.

tools.name: ovf_import
tools.description: Start an OVF/OVA import into a NEW VM directory. Supports typed network/property mappings and explicit EULA acceptance. Registration through REST and headless power-on are opt-in. Returns a job ID; poll job_status.

tools.name: ovf_export
tools.description: Start a powered-off VMX export to OVF/OVA. Refuses snapshots, locks, saved state, external backings, encryption and vTPM. OVF needs a new parent directory. Only OVA permits explicit overwrite=true. Returns a job ID.

tools.name: ovf_convert
tools.description: Start a local OVF/OVA/VMX conversion using VMware OVF Tool. VMX sources require power-off and no snapshots. OVF/VMX targets need new parent directories; overwrite is limited to OVA. Returns a job ID.

tools.name: job_start
tools.description: Start a bounded background job of explicit disk conversion/expansion, full offline cloning or headless VM power steps. Requires confirm=true for every target and action. Steps run sequentially and stop on failure; separate unrelated jobs run concurrently. Returns a job ID; inspect status, partial results and artifact paths before retrying.

tools.name: job_status
tools.description: Read background state, genuine backend progress and verified result/error from private bounded journals. Unfinished prior-session jobs report interrupted with unknown outcome and are never replayed.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List up to 100 current and retained historical jobs from private redacted journals, retained for at most seven days. History does not imply a previous process has stopped.

tools.name: job_cancel
tools.description: Request cancellation of a current job and its native process tree. Locks remain until process cleanup finishes. Partial files and VM changes may remain; inspect before retrying.

tools.name: job_logs
tools.description: Read bounded, redacted background job output. Raw probe metadata/property defaults are omitted. A truncated log is explicitly marked.

tools.name: list_lan_segments
tools.description: List the current host user LAN segment catalog. Optionally supply vmx to inspect adapter indices and segment associations, including orphaned IDs. Does not scan disks or change VMs.

tools.name: create_lan_segment
tools.description: Create a named private LAN segment in Workstation preferences with a backup, or return the uniquely named existing segment. Close the Workstation/Player GUI first. Does not create a VMnet, DHCP server or VM adapter.

tools.name: remove_lan_segment
tools.description: Remove a LAN segment from Workstation preferences with a backup. Refuses references in registered/running and supplied unregistered VMX files; detach those adapters first. Cannot discover other unregistered VMs. Close the Workstation/Player GUI first.

tools.name: attach_vm_adapter_to_lan_segment
tools.description: Attach an existing powered-off VM adapter to a LAN segment. adapter is the zero-based ethernetN index. Backs up the UTF-8 VMX, clears any custom VMnet, and enables connection at next power-on. Close the Workstation/Player GUI first.

tools.name: detach_vm_adapter_from_lan_segment
tools.description: Detach an existing powered-off VM adapter from the specified LAN segment, preserving the adapter. Backs up the UTF-8 VMX, removes its segment ID, selects a replacement network (default NAT), and leaves the adapter disconnected at next power-on. Close the Workstation/Player GUI first.

tools.name: workstation_status
tools.description: Check local vmrun availability and count running VMs without changing them.

tools.name: list_vms
tools.description: List registered and running VMs. Stale inventory entries are retained and marked. This does not scan disks.

tools.name: get_vm_details
tools.description: Read selected VM hardware configuration and whether the VM is running. Does not expose the full VMX.

tools.name: vm_power
tools.description: Start, gracefully stop, reset, suspend, pause or unpause a VM. Defaults to soft mode. Hard stop/reset can lose data; use only when explicitly requested. No automatic hard fallback.

tools.name: list_snapshots
tools.description: List snapshot names without changing the VM.

tools.name: create_snapshot
tools.description: Create a named snapshot on the selected VM. Requires a user request to create it.

tools.name: revert_snapshot
tools.description: Revert the VM to an existing snapshot. Discards later VM state; requires explicit user authorization for this VM and snapshot.

tools.name: delete_snapshot
tools.description: Delete one named snapshot, preserving children. Removes a restore point; requires explicit user authorization for this VM and snapshot.

tools.name: get_guest_ip
tools.description: Get the IP address reported by VMware Tools in a running VM. Optional wait=true uses a bounded native wait; timeout_seconds defaults to 120. No guest login, power changes or automatic retries.

tools.name: plugin_catalog
tools.description: Read running plugin version, process identity and complete registered tool names without VMware or credentials. Optionally compare assistant-visible names to diagnose missing tools, including an alphabetical cutoff. Cannot refresh the client catalog.

tools.name: vmrun_start
tools.description: Start a VM; optionally show its Workstation window.

tools.name: vmrun_stop
tools.description: stop a VM. Soft mode is the default; hard mode requires explicit authorization.

tools.name: vmrun_reset
tools.description: reset a VM. Soft mode is the default; hard mode requires explicit authorization.

tools.name: vmrun_suspend
tools.description: suspend a VM. Soft mode is the default; hard mode requires explicit authorization.

tools.name: vmrun_pause
tools.description: pause a VM.

tools.name: vmrun_unpause
tools.description: unpause a VM.

tools.name: vmrun_list_snapshots
tools.description: List VM snapshots; show_tree returns the hierarchy.

tools.name: vmrun_snapshot
tools.description: Create a named VM snapshot.

tools.name: vmrun_delete_snapshot
tools.description: Delete a named snapshot. Optionally delete its children as explicitly requested.

tools.name: vmrun_revert_to_snapshot
tools.description: Revert to a named snapshot; later VM state is discarded.

tools.name: vmrun_list_host_networks
tools.description: List VMware virtual host networks.

tools.name: vmrun_list_port_forwardings
tools.description: List port forwarding rules on a host network.

tools.name: vmrun_set_port_forwarding
tools.description: Add or update a host network port forwarding rule.

tools.name: vmrun_delete_port_forwarding
tools.description: Delete a host network port forwarding rule.

tools.name: vmrun_run_program_in_guest
tools.description: Execute a program in the guest. This returns vmrun status, not guest stdout or a reliable guest program exit code.

tools.name: vmrun_file_exists_in_guest
tools.description: Check whether a guest file exists.

tools.name: vmrun_directory_exists_in_guest
tools.description: Check whether a guest directory exists.

tools.name: vmrun_set_shared_folder_state
tools.description: Set a shared folder host path and write access.

tools.name: vmrun_add_shared_folder
tools.description: Add a host directory as a guest shared folder.

tools.name: vmrun_remove_shared_folder
tools.description: Remove a shared folder mapping.

tools.name: vmrun_enable_shared_folders
tools.description: Enable shared folders; runtime_only avoids a persistent change.

tools.name: vmrun_disable_shared_folders
tools.description: Disable shared folders.

tools.name: vmrun_list_processes_in_guest
tools.description: List guest processes.

tools.name: vmrun_kill_process_in_guest
tools.description: Terminate a guest process by process ID.

tools.name: vmrun_run_script_in_guest
tools.description: Run script text with a guest interpreter. Redirect script output to a guest file and copy it back if output is needed.

tools.name: vmrun_delete_file_in_guest
tools.description: Delete a guest file.

tools.name: vmrun_create_directory_in_guest
tools.description: Create a guest directory.

tools.name: vmrun_delete_directory_in_guest
tools.description: Delete a guest directory.

tools.name: vmrun_create_tempfile_in_guest
tools.description: Create a temporary file in the guest.

tools.name: vmrun_list_directory_in_guest
tools.description: List a guest directory.

tools.name: vmrun_copy_file_from_host_to_guest
tools.description: Copy a local host file to a guest path. The destination may be overwritten by VMware.

tools.name: vmrun_copy_file_from_guest_to_host
tools.description: Copy a guest file to a local host path. Existing host files are protected unless overwrite=true.

tools.name: vmrun_rename_file_in_guest
tools.description: Rename a guest file.

tools.name: vmrun_type_keystrokes_in_guest
tools.description: Type text into the guest console.

tools.name: vmrun_connect_named_device
tools.description: Connect a named virtual device.

tools.name: vmrun_disconnect_named_device
tools.description: Disconnect a named virtual device.

tools.name: vmrun_capture_screen
tools.description: Capture the VM display into a local file.

tools.name: vmrun_write_variable
tools.description: Write a VM runtimeConfig, guestEnv, or guestVar variable.

tools.name: vmrun_read_variable
tools.description: Read a VM runtimeConfig, guestEnv, or guestVar variable.

tools.name: vmrun_get_guest_ip_address
tools.description: Read the guest address reported by VMware Tools; optionally wait until available.

tools.name: vmrun_list
tools.description: List running VMX paths.

tools.name: vmrun_upgradevm
tools.description: Upgrade a VM virtual hardware/file format.

tools.name: vmrun_install_tools
tools.description: Start VMware Tools installation in the guest.

tools.name: vmrun_check_tools_state
tools.description: Inspect VMware Tools state.

tools.name: vmrun_delete_vm
tools.description: Delete the selected VM and its VMware-managed files. Requires explicit authorization for the exact VM.

tools.name: vmrun_clone
tools.description: Create a full or linked clone of a VM, optionally from a named snapshot.

tools.name: vmrun_download_photon_vm
tools.description: Download a Photon template VM into a selected host directory.

tools.name: workstation_capabilities
tools.description: Show full vmrun/REST tool coverage, compare the installed vmrun help against the implemented catalog, and report REST configuration without exposing secrets.

tools.name: plugin_query
tools.description: Call a discovered read-only VMware operation when its direct tool is missing. First use plugin_catalog with tool to obtain the original strict argument schema. Reuses the same handler, deadlines, cancellation and redaction. Cannot call mutations or arbitrary commands; never bypass intentional policy.

tools.name: plugin_mutate
tools.description: Call a discovered state-changing VMware operation when its direct tool is missing. First obtain its schema from plugin_catalog. Requires authorization for exact target/effects, confirm=true and every original confirmation. Reuses original validation, locks, credentials and handler; never retries. Do not bypass intentional policy.

credentials_file.title: Credentials file
credentials_file.description: Optional absolute path to the existing private credentials JSON. Leave blank to use your per-user default.

vmrun_path.title: vmrun executable
vmrun_path.description: Optional absolute native vmrun executable path. Leave blank for automatic discovery.

vmcli_path.title: vmcli executable
vmcli_path.description: Optional absolute vmcli executable path for read-only capability inspection.

vmx_path.title: VMware worker executable
vmx_path.description: Optional absolute vmware-vmx executable path for native worker verification.

inventory_path.title: VM inventory
inventory_path.description: Optional absolute inventory.vmls path. Leave blank for the current user inventory.

preferences_path.title: VMware preferences
preferences_path.description: Optional absolute preferences file path for LAN segment configuration.

allowed_roots.title: Allowed VM directories
allowed_roots.description: Optional absolute directories separated by semicolons on Windows or colons on Linux. Blank preserves inherited policy or existing unrestricted defaults. Inventory still lists paths outside these roots.

allowed_host_roots.title: Allowed host directories
allowed_host_roots.description: Optional absolute directories for host files, separated by semicolons on Windows or colons on Linux. Blank preserves inherited policy or existing defaults.

rest_url.title: REST origin
rest_url.description: Optional VMware REST origin. Default: http://127.0.0.1:8697. Remote services require HTTPS. Credentials stay in the local credentials file.
